Fine-Gray Subdistribution Hazard Model, Fitted for Prediction

Source: R/fine_gray_predict.R
fine_gray.Rd

Fits the Fine-Gray (1999) proportional subdistribution hazards model of one cause with the other causes treated as competing events, using `cmprsk::crr()`, and keeps the fit so [predict.fine_gray_model()] can return the predicted cumulative incidence function (CIF). It is the fitted-model counterpart of [tbl_fine_gray_multi()], which returns a coefficient table only: the design matrix, factor levels and event codes are stored here, so new data are encoded the same way as the training data.

Usage

fine_gray(data, time_col, event_col, formula, failcode = 1, cencode = 0, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fine_gray_model'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per subject.

time_col

Follow-up time.

event_col

Event type, as in [tbl_cumulative_incidence()]: a censoring code, then one code per cause.

formula

One-sided formula of the predictors, for example `~ age + arm + sex`.

failcode

Code of the cause of interest (default 1).

cencode

Code for censoring (default 0).

...

Passed to `cmprsk::crr()` (for example `maxiter`). Prediction works whether `variance` is `TRUE` or `FALSE`: `crr()` stores the baseline hazard either way.

x

The object to print (the result of the function).

Value

An object of class `fine_gray_model` with the `crr` fit (`$fit`), the design matrix (`$x`), the model terms and factor levels (`$terms`, `$xlevels`), the event codes (`$failcode`, `$cencode`), and `n` / `n_event` (rows used / events of the cause of interest) / `n_dropped` (rows dropped for missing values; a warning reports the count when it is not zero).

Details

The CIF for covariates `x` is `1 - exp(-exp(x'b) * H0(t))`, where `H0` is the baseline cumulative subdistribution hazard, evaluated by `cmprsk::predict.crr()` at the event times of the cause of interest. A competing event keeps a subject in the risk set, which is what `crr()` does; the CIF is therefore the probability of the cause of interest by time `t` in the presence of the competing causes, not a Kaplan-Meier risk.

See also

[predict.fine_gray_model()], [predict_fine_gray()], [tbl_fine_gray_multi()], [tbl_fine_gray_single()], [tbl_cumulative_incidence()]

Examples

if (requireNamespace("cmprsk", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  d <- data.frame(time = rexp(150, 0.1), type = sample(0:2, 150, TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.3)),
                  age = rnorm(150, 60, 8), arm = rep(c("A", "B"), 75))
  fit <- fine_gray(d, "time", "type", ~ age + arm)
  fit
  predict(fit, d[1:3, ])
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   .pred            
#>   <list>           
#> 1 <tibble [69 × 2]>
#> 2 <tibble [69 × 2]>
#> 3 <tibble [69 × 2]>
